title: Keep production values; compare floats in tests
summary: Illustrative example only—not a review of a real MR. We remove rounding from production and let tests handle floating-point comparison tolerance instead. These edits belong together: the application should not change its results merely to satisfy a test assertion.
context: In this fictional service, a calculation produces a numeric result consumed by an API caller. Previously the return boundary rounded that result. The calculation and API shape stay the same; the caller now receives the unrounded value. Tests compare significant figures instead of expecting exact float equality.

diagrams.title: Before: production rounds the result
diagrams.explanation: Illustrative old path. The red box and arrows identify the rounding behavior being removed—not behavior that remains in the new path. Click the rounding box to inspect the deletion.

diagrams.title: After: preserve values; compare tolerantly in tests
diagrams.explanation: The green arrow bypasses the deleted rounding step. The new green test helper compares the result without changing the API response. Grey boxes are existing context. Select a colored box to see its code example.

themes.title: Return the calculated value without rounding
themes.explanation: The production change is a deletion, not a new processing stage. Removing the rounding step preserves the calculated value. For example, a calculated 1.234567 would previously return 1.2346 and now returns 1.234567. Both the code and numbers here are illustrative.

examples.title: Delete rounding at the return boundary
examples.explanation: Illustrative pseudocode, not an excerpt from MR !332. The calculation is unchanged; only rounding is removed.

themes.title: Move comparison tolerance into the tests
themes.explanation: The tests still check the expected number, but no longer require exact binary floating-point equality. A significant-figure comparison is a test policy, not a transformation of the API response. Choosing the precision remains important: too few significant figures could hide a real regression.

examples.title: Compare at the declared significant figures
examples.explanation: Illustrative pseudocode only. A real review should quote the actual helper and assertion, explain its precision, and check zero, signs, very small values, and non-finite values where relevant.
examples.after:
compareSignificantFigures({ actual, expected, figures: precision })

compareSignificantFigures({ actual, expected, figures }):
  assert actual and expected are finite
  assert actual.toPrecision(figures) == expected.toPrecision(figures)

sections.title: What a real review would verify
sections.explanation: Confirm the full diff removes all intended rounding, that consumers can accept unrounded values, and that the tests still catch meaningful numeric errors. Map any supplied acceptance criteria to code and test evidence. The optional before/after diagrams illustrate the delta without mapping unrelated architecture. This example is not evidence that any real MR meets those criteria.
